title: EPIM: Efficient Processing-In-Memory Accelerators based on Epitome
problem: Large-scale neural networks on Processing-In-Memory (PIM) accelerators face constrained on-chip memory capacity. Most existing approaches use generic model compression techniques like quantization or neural architecture search without designing operators specifically optimized for PIM accelerator constraints.
motivation: PIM accelerators offer energy-efficient neural network processing, but memory limitations prevent deployment of large-scale CNNs without specialized operator design.
method: The paper introduces Epitome, a lightweight neural operator providing convolution-like functionality optimized for PIM architectures. On software: PIM-aware layer-wise design and epitome-aware 3-bit quantization reduce model size. On hardware: the PIM datapath is modified to support epitomes and feature map reuse techniques reduce computation cost.
key_novelty: Introduction of Epitome as a PIM-specific lightweight neural operator that trades expressiveness for memory efficiency while maintaining CNN compatibility.
contributions: Epitome neural operator designed specifically for PIM accelerator memory and computation constraints
PIM-aware layer-wise design methodology for optimizing operator efficiency
Epitome-aware quantization achieving 3-bit precision while preserving accuracy
Hardware modifications with feature map reuse achieving 30.65X crossbar area reduction
primary_theme: PIM-optimized lightweight neural operators for CNN inference
